slides.title: While Loop Basics
slides.content: A while loop repeats a block of code while a condition remains true. It checks the condition before each iteration.

exercise.prompt: When does a while loop check its condition?

slides.title: Loop Condition
slides.content: The condition must be a bool expression. If it starts as false, the loop body never runs.
slides.exampleOutput: No output: the loop condition is false, so the body never runs.

exercise.prompt: If the condition is false initially, the loop body runs _____ times

slides.title: Incrementing
slides.content: Loops usually need an update statement inside the body to eventually stop. Forgetting it creates an infinite loop.

exercise.prompt: Complete the while loop to count to 2

slides.title: Infinite Loops
slides.content: An infinite loop never ends because its condition never becomes false. Use break to exit manually if needed.

exercise.prompt: Which condition creates an infinite loop?

slides.title: Do-While Loop
slides.content: A do-while loop runs its body at least once because the condition is checked after the body.

exercise.prompt: A do-while always executes its body _____ times

slides.title: Do-While Syntax
slides.content: The do-while loop places the condition after the body, terminated with a semicolon. Braces are required when the body has multiple statements.

slides.title: Loop Counters
slides.content: A counter variable tracks how many times the loop has run. Initialize it before the loop and update it inside.

exercise.prompt: Use a while loop to print numbers 2, 4, 6 using int n = 2

// Write your while loop below
hints: Make sure your code includes the required keywords/elements: while, Console.WriteLine

slides.title: While with Strings
slides.content: You can use while loops to process strings character by character until reaching the end.

exercise.prompt: The loop stops when index _____ word.Length

slides.title: Nested While Loops
slides.content: A while loop can contain another while loop. The inner loop must complete before the outer loop continues.

exercise.prompt: How many times does the inner loop run if outer=1 and inner<=2?

slides.title: Break and Continue
slides.content: break exits the loop immediately. continue skips the rest of the current iteration and re-evaluates the condition.

exercise.prompt: Complete the loop to skip even numbers

slides.content: Use the Flow Builder to create a while loop that counts to 2.
